question: What is the difference in molecular mass between two successive members of a homologous series?
solution:
The correct answer is __**14u**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
• A **homologous series** is a group of **organic compounds** that have the same **functional group** and similar **chemical properties**, in which successive members differ by a **CH2 unit**. 
• In any homologous series, the difference in the **molecular formula** between two consecutive members is always **-CH2-** (methylene group). 
• The **molecular mass** of a compound is the sum of the **atomic masses** of all the atoms present in its molecule. 
• The **atomic mass** of **Carbon (C)** is **12u** and the **atomic mass** of **Hydrogen (H)** is **1u**. 
• Therefore, the mass of a **CH2 unit** is calculated as: **12 + (2 × 1) = 14u**. ***Hence, the difference in molecular mass between two successive members is 14u.***
